messages:
Jordan: quick sync on the PRD -> RFC handoff for the kernel + KV cache + attention perf changes. want to lock launch gates and acceptance criteria today.
Anya: 👍 need to prioritize customer asks vs platform risk. which customers are driving the kernel switch?
Kevin: three customers: FinReg (latency & determinism), SocialX (cost), and Searchly (long-prefix perf). FinReg is strict on tail latency and bounded jitter.
Maria: notable edge case: long conversation histories (>64k tokens) cause KV cache thrash with current eviction. we need explicit acceptance for streaming continuity.
Eli: proposal from runtime team: default to LRU+pinning for pinned prefixes, plus a soft quota per-request to avoid thrash. draft PRD snippet:

```
Acceptance Criteria:
- 99.9th percentile latency for 2k token requests <= 220ms on c6g-equivalent hardware under 80% load.
- KV cache hit rate >= 85% for pinned prefixes from customer-visible sessions.
- Rollout toggle to revert to legacy kernel in <5 minutes without loss of in-flight streams.
```

Jordan: that latency number looks optimistic for some models — which model families were used for estimation?
Kevin: baseline used: redwood/llama-like-13b-qat and a trimmed-attn kernel. we'll add conservative margin in PRD.
Anya: can we add a customer-facing SLO and an internal quality gate? e.g., automated evals on a small prompt set of customer traffic patterns.
Maria: yes. add regression detection: perf or output quality degradation triggers canary hold and rollback.
Eli: edge cases to list in RFC: mixed-precision + quantized kernels, streaming token boundary mismatches, failure during KV restore, pinned prefix evictions.
Jordan: okay. for scope: MVP should include kernel selection logic, simple KV pinning API, and rollout controls. postponing autotuner for later.
Kevin: timeline estimate: RFC complete by end of week, implementation + canary in 3 sprint cycles, full rollout after 2-week canary.
Anya: prioritization: is this Critical for the next release? customers flagged FinReg as blocker for Dedicated onboarding.
Jordan: mark as P0 for Dedicated onboarding only; P1 for Hosted. we'll update roadmap accordingly.
Maria: acceptance test matrix idea:
- unit tests for eviction correctness
- load test with synthetic long-prefix traces
- canary against a low-traffic customer with real flows
- automated evals for output drift

InfraBot: scheduled test cluster spin-up at 2026-03-22T09:00Z for canary runs :gear:
Eli: doc ask: who owns the PRD -> RFC merge? want a single owner for follow-ups.
Jordan: I'll own the PRD. Kevin + Maria co-own the runtime RFC. Anya will own rollout & customer comms.
Anya: I'll draft the customer-facing note with rollback expectations and UX during canary.
Kevin: adding one more acceptance edge case: model-switch fallback — if selected kernel is incompatible, auto-route to last-good variant without dropping request.
Maria: note: ensure metrics include cross-model comparators, not just per-kernel. that's how we detect quality regressions.
Jordan: thanks. action items:
- Kevin: finish RFC with edge cases + kernel selection heuristics (due Thu)
- Maria: write eviction tests + long-prefix load scenario (due next Tue)
- Anya: comms + customer gating list (due Thu)
- Eli: add regression eval harness to CI (due next Wed)
- Jordan: update PRD launch gates doc and Slack thread (due Fri)

Jordan: any blockers?
Kevin: need access to FinReg traces (PII-safe subset). Anya is coordinating.
Anya: I have grant request in flight.
Maria: otherwise good. let's reconvene after RFC draft review.
Jordan: cool — posting RFC draft in #eng-runtime when ready. :eyes:
